- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for early spikes.
- After a strong downward spike (e.g., >5% drop), model often fails to rebound quickly; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in next 5–7 days if sentiment turns bullish.
- If supply net is negative and events are frequent (≥20/30d), model overestimates mean reversion; shift forecast upward by 1–2% to account for persistent bearish sentiment.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to smooth out volatility; increase forecast volatility by ±0.5–1.0% to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
- If model shows steady upward trend (e.g., +0.1–0.3% per day) but true outcome shows sharp reversal, reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.2% per day for next 3–5 days.
- For auctions with high supply net (e.g., CAP3 EU), model often underestimates price impact; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment is bullish or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to match sentiment swing direction 1–2 days ahead.
